correctness.rationale: The cited primary preprint supplies uniform concentration of the numerator around a center tending to one, uniform concentration of the normalized sup-norm denominator about its mean with \(\mathbb E V\to1\), and the deterministic ratio bound \(R_m\le N_{m,n}^{1/(2m)}\). Hence \(0\le Y_{m,n}\le\sqrt{H_{m,n}}\). On the good event, \(|Y-1|\) is uniformly small; on the bad event, the polynomial envelope \((1+\sqrt H)^s\) is dominated by the source's exponential tails because \(H\to\infty\) and \(N/H\to\infty\) uniformly. This proves uniform \(L^s\) convergence. Radial-angular independence transfers the Gaussian statement to the coefficient sphere. The endpoint \(n=2\), where \(H\) grows slowest, still has exponential tail domination.
